title: The time of arrival problem in the Page-Wootters formalism
version: arXiv:2604.00092v1 (submitted 2026-03-31; only version listed on the abstract page 2026-10-20). Not refereed as far as the abstract page shows.
locators: Sec. II.2 last paragraph (sector-wise reduction for degenerate clock Hamiltonian; partial isometries); Sec. II.3 Eqs. (15)-(20) and the sentence after Eq. (20) (superselection claim); Sec. III.1 paragraph 2 (naive map R~(x0) not invertible, 'cannot be normalised in a state-independent manner'); Sec. III.1 Eqs. (23)-(27) and footnote 1 (sector-wise position states, partial isometry, inverse Eq. 26, normalisation sum over sigma); Sec. III.2 Eqs. (28)-(30) (sector-mixed arrival-time rule = Kijowski); Sec. IV after Eq. (32) (naive rule 'neither unity nor normalisable in a manner independent of' the physical state); Sec. V footnote 3 (coherence permitted relative to the clock); Sec. V paragraphs 2-4 (falsifiability by interference; separation persists under modified conditions); Appendix A Eqs. (33)-(46) (general single-map reduction R(y)=1_C x <y|_S; many-to-one; isometry only per sector; iff form Eq. 42; inverse Eq. 46).
assumptions: Uncoupled clock and free particle, C = H_C x 1 + 1 x p^2/2m (Eq. 14); non-degenerate clock Hamiltonian with R_- contained in spec(H_C) (Sec. II.3); the sigma label is the sign of the particle momentum (system degeneracy), with a sign convention different from 2007.00580; conditioning on a system property y via rank-one maps R(y)=1_C x <y|_S (Appendix A); isometry of each single map demanded (Eq. 39); spatial translation covariance (Eq. 24) and covariant clock POVM.
conclusion: Authors' claims: a single reduction map conditioning on a system property cannot be isometric across both momentum sectors; reduction must be sector-wise (partial isometries) and is fixed up to phase by translation covariance; the resulting normalised arrival-time distribution Eq. (30) coincides with Kijowski's and forbids interference between counter-propagating wavepackets, which the authors present as an empirical falsifier. They also argue the conditional-probability reading of Page-Wootters has complications (Sec. IV).
proof_status: Appendix A proof read line by line at the level of the HTML rendering; not independently re-derived. Eq. (37) as rendered in the HTML has r(y, p_sigma) in the second factor where p_sigma' would be expected; PDF not checked.
dependencies: frontier-relativistic-trinity-2020v1 (their ref. [32]); Bartlett-Rudolph-Spekkens (their ref. [7]) cited for the superselection reading; Trinity 1912.00033 (their ref. [33], Eq. 43 cited in footnote 3); Kijowski 1974.
open_questions: Appendix A only treats a single rank-one conditioning map per y; a family of two maps {R_b(y)} each with support on both sectors but jointly isometric is not addressed. Footnote 3 says coherence across momentum sectors is permitted relative to the clock; how this squares with the Sec. II.3 statement that expectation values are insensitive to the coherence is not spelled out beyond a pointer to Eq. (43) of 1912.00033.
relevance: Primary source for the state-independent normalisation failure of the plain (naive) reduction map, the single-map isometry no-go, and the sector-mixed normalised rule; nearest predecessor for RC-3 sector-coherent conditioning.
limits: Free particle, position conditioning on a non-degenerate clock; not the relativistic quadratic clock C_H = s p_t^2/2 + H_S. No external or internal phase reference is modelled anywhere in the paper. Math transcribed from LaTeXML alttext.

title: Reference frames, superselection rules, and quantum information
version: arXiv:quant-ph/0610030v3 (2007-04-10); published Rev. Mod. Phys. 79, 555 (2007), DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.79.555. Read from arXiv v3 HTML; the RMP typeset version was not read.
locators: Sec. II.1 (RFs and group G; footnote 1 coset case); Sec. II.2 Eqs. (1)-(13) and the two paragraphs after Eq. (13) (photon-number SSR from lacking a phase reference; SSR restricts Alice only); Sec. II.3 Eqs. (14)-(26), Theorem and proof (compact or finite groups; G-twirl; observables-only SSR remark); Sec. IV introduction; Sec. IV.1.1 Eqs. (76)-(86) (quantised internal phase reference, wall analogy); Sec. IV.1.2 Eqs. (87)-(91) (dequantisation, relational Hilbert space); Sec. IV.1.3 (optical coherence controversy); Sec. IV.1.4 Eqs. (92)-(93); Sec. IV.2 Eqs. (94)-(106) ($-map; unbounded RF; footnote 11 finite groups); Sec. IV.3; Sec. VII Outlook paragraph on non-compact groups.
assumptions: SSRs arising from G-twirling over a compact Lie group or a finite group acting by a unitary representation (Sec. II.3); the quantised RF carries a regular representation with perfectly distinguishable orientation states, requiring infinite dimension for Lie groups (Eqs. 98-99).
conclusion: Authors' claims: lacking a shared RF for G is equivalent to an SSR for G; an internal quantum RF R makes the composite RS description G-invariant yet reproduces all statistics of the SSR-free description ($-map, Eq. 106); hence 'all superselection rules associated with unitary representations of compact groups result from a lack of an appropriate reference frame'. Non-compact groups (Lorentz, Poincare) are explicitly left to 'more general mathematical tools'.
proof_status: Theorem proof (Schur lemmas) and the $-map algebra (Eqs. 104-106) read and followed; standard results, not re-derived independently.
dependencies: Aharonov-Susskind 1967; Wick-Wightman-Wigner; Kitaev-Mayers-Preskill (ref. [118] there) for the lifting construction.
open_questions: The framework presupposes that the SSR comes from twirling over a compact or finite group. The sigma-sector superselection of 2007.00580 is said by its authors not to come from the (non-compact, R) group generated by the constraint; whether it can be recast as a Z2 SSR generated by the sector operator Q and then lifted by an internal Z2 reference system that is itself gauge-invariant under C_H is not addressed in this review (our question).
relevance: The framework 2007.00580 cites (ref. [117]) for 'lifting' a superselection rule with a reference frame; it treats internal, quantised, gauge(G)-invariant reference systems, but only for compact or finite G and outside any Hamiltonian-constraint setting.
limits: Sections II, IV (all subsections IV.1-IV.3) and the Outlook paragraph read; Secs. III, V, VI only skimmed by heading (except V.8 opening). No discussion of Hamiltonian constraints, Page-Wootters clocks, or frequency sectors.

title: Relational Dynamics with Periodic Clocks
locators: Abstract; Sec. II.2 paragraph and footnote 2 (energy-independent clock degeneracy); Sec. III footnote 10 (degenerate clocks handled 'per degeneracy sector, as in [11, 16]'); Sec. IV.2 Example 9 Eq. (63) and Example 10 Eqs. (64)-(65) (left/right movers H_phys = L2_+ (+) L2_-; qubit H_phys = C^2); Sec. V intro paragraph on isotropy groups; Sec. V.2 Example 13 Eqs. (78)-(81) and Example 14 (Dirac observable algebra L(H_phys)); Sec. VI.1 Eqs. (82)-(90), Lemma 8; Sec. VI.2.1 Eqs. (91)-(101), Lemma 9; Sec. VI.2.2 Theorem 2; Sec. VI.2.3 Theorem 3, Corollary 3; Sec. VI.2.4 conditional probability definition, Lemma 10, Eq. (106).
assumptions: Periodic clock with discrete non-degenerate spectrum (degenerate case deferred to footnote 10); constraint may generate R (non-compact) while the clock generates U(1); for the free-particle examples the two-fold degeneracy is in the system (momentum sign), not in the clock.
conclusion: Authors' claims: trinity holds for periodic clocks; the PW map R_S(tau) = <tau| x I_S is an isometry onto the physical system Hilbert space (Corollary 3); every quantum Dirac observable is the relational observable of some physical system observable; the kinematical-inner-product conditional probability diverges when the constraint generates R (Lemma 10, Eq. 106) and must be replaced by the physical-inner-product rule of Sec. VI.2.4. For the left/right-mover examples a single non-sector-wise reduction is used and the Dirac algebra is stated to be all of L(H_phys) (Example 14).
proof_status: Statements read; proofs are in Appendix B, not read.
dependencies: frontier-relativistic-trinity-2020v1 (ref. [11]); frontier-relational-trinity-2019v3 (ref. [10]); de la Hamette et al. 2110.13824 (ref. [12]); De Vuyst et al. 2412.15502 (ref. [16]).
open_questions: Hosseini-Lock (Sec. V) cite this paper's Example 9 for the persistence of non-interference between left and right movers, but Example 9 itself only states the direct-sum decomposition, while Examples 13-14 count sector-mixing operators (for example the projected position, Eq. 81, as rendered with a coherent sum over mu = +/-1) as Dirac observables. Whether the two statements concern different observable algebras (clock-time versus position conditioning) is not settled by the texts read.
relevance: The left/right-mover treatment named in the brief; shows that with a non-degenerate reference clock the system's momentum-sign sectors are not treated as superselected, and gives the physical-inner-product conditional probability rule.
limits: Appendices and Sec. VII not read. Eq. (81) as rendered writes |p=p_n> while the phase carries mu; PDF not checked. Degenerate-clock periodic case only mentioned in footnote 10.
